To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there is a plausible, but not proven climate conflict link in the case of Syria, and that the link is not as clear cut as often portrayed in the media.

the 2006 2010 drought likely contributed to the onset of the Syrian civil war by increasing rural to urban migration, which in turn increased the vulnerability of the rural population to the political crisis and facilitated the onset of protests.

the Syrian drought did not cause the civil war, but that the drought did increase the likelihood of the war by increasing the vulnerability of the rural population and by facilitating the onset of the conflict.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether climate change can be a driver of violent conflict.
the question of how the Syrian case can contribute to a more productive and useful climate conflict research agenda.
the question of how we can best contribute to an improved dialogue between climate and conflict research.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a plausible link between drought, migration and the Syrian civil war.
the drought likely aggravated the Syrian conflict, but it cannot be said that the drought was the sole cause of the conflict or that climate change caused the Syrian civil war.
the drought was an important, but not sufficient, cause of the civil war.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
climate change may be a contributing factor to the Syrian civil war, but it is far from the sole or even the main cause.
the drought did not directly cause the civil war.
the Syrian case is an example for the potential of climate change to contribute to conflict, but that the evidence is still too weak to make any definitive statements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Syrian civil war cannot be attributed to climate change, and that the debate on the Syrian case has contributed to an overstatement of potential climate conflict links.
the climate conflict link for the Syrian case remains speculative, and more research is needed to establish the link.
the Syrian case is an important case study for climate conflict research, and that it should not be used to draw general conclusions about climate change and conflict.
